text.p: Nigerian shares were steady on Thursday with dealing mostly driven by speculation, traders said.
The all share index closed at 6654.52 from 6654.53 on Wednesday.
Traders dismissed an unconfirmed local newspaper report that Nigeria's military government may have signed a decree allowing it to acquire golden shares in the nation's four biggest banks.
Such action would be contrary to government's decision to privatise key sectors of the Nigerian economy, another said.
Two of the banks, United Bank for Africa rose two kobo to 5.07 naira while Union Bank fell by 10 kobo to 7.10 naira.
Mixed trading pervaded the breweries and cement sectors.
While Nigerian Breweries consolidated its gain with 30 kobo to 11.00 naira, Guinness slumped 10 kobo to 6.70 naira.
West African Portland Cement ended at 38.00 naira, up 20 kobo, but Ashaka Cement and Benue Cement Company fell three kobo and two kobo, respectively, to 19.47 naira and 7.30 naira.
Conglomerates Lever Brothers and CFAO were five kobo down at 25.20 naira and 3.90 naira, respectively. UTC was the sole gainer in the sector, climbing two kobo to 82 kobo.
Most food shares were up on increased demand, traders said.
Nestle went 40 kobo higher at 40.00 naira, National Salt added five kobo to 5.75 naira and P.S. Mandrides gained two kobo to 2.67 naira. Flour Mills fell 20 kobo to 10.80 naira.
Oil marketers also advanced in speculative trade. Unipetrol was Thursday's biggest gainer, up 68 kobo at 47.00 naira.
Mobil was 20 kobo up at 42.80 naira, National Oil rose 18 kobo to 38.60 naira, Texaco notched 13 to 28.30 naira and Agip rose five to 15.85 naira. Total was unchanged at 50.15 naira.
